title: Macros and result builders
summary: Result builders turn a list of statements into one value (that is how SwiftUI `body` works). Macros generate Swift code at compile time (`@Observable`, `#Preview`).
body: **In simple words:** Both features remove boilerplate. A **result builder** lets you write a list of things in a closure and the compiler combines them; in SwiftUI, writing `Text("a"); Text("b")` inside a `VStack` becomes one combined view. A **macro** is a code generator: you write `@Observable` and the compiler writes the tracking code for you.
**Result builders:** a type marked `@resultBuilder` with static methods like `buildBlock`, `buildOptional` (for `if`), `buildEither` (for `if/else`), `buildArray` (for `for`). `@ViewBuilder` is one.

**Macros (Swift 5.9+):** two kinds - **freestanding** start with `#` (`#Preview`, `#expect`) and **attached** start with `@` (`@Observable`, `@Model`). They can only add code, not secretly change yours, and Xcode can "Expand Macro" to show what they generate.
**Staff-level view:** macros cost build time and can be hard to debug. Use them to remove error-prone boilerplate, not to hide business logic.
keyPoints: Result builder = closure statements combined into one value (SwiftUI `@ViewBuilder`).
`@Observable` expands into property tracking code using an `ObservationRegistrar`.
Use "Expand Macro" in Xcode to see generated code; watch build-time impact.

followups: **How does `if` work inside a SwiftUI body?** The builder's `buildEither` produces `_ConditionalContent` holding one of two branches.
**Can a macro access other files or the network?** No, macros run sandboxed and only see the syntax they are attached to.
